hindi: वर्णित चौरासी आसवों की तथा पीने योग्य और न पीने योग्य जल की परीक्षा करके हितकर (पेय) को (भोजन के) बाद पीना चाहिए।
english: Having examined the eighty-four āsavas that have been described, and water fit and unfit to drink, one should drink afterwards what is wholesome.
notes: caturuttarām aśītim = 'eighty with four more', i.e. eighty-four. anupibet 'should drink after' (the meal), whence anupāna.

hindi: मारुत में स्निग्ध और उष्ण, पित्त में मधुर और शीतल, कफ में रूक्ष और उष्ण अनुपान प्रशस्त है; क्षय में मांसरस श्रेष्ठ है।
english: In Vāta (māruta) an unctuous and hot after-drink (anupāna) is commended, in Pitta a sweet and cold one, in Kapha a dry and hot one; in wasting (kṣaya) meat-juice is the best.
notes: anupānam (in line b) and śastam are understood with all three doṣas. param 'best' is neuter though māṃsarasaḥ is masculine; read as the predicate 'the best (thing)'.

words.gloss: by fasting, travel, speaking, women, wind, sun and action

hindi: उपवास, मार्ग-गमन, बोलने, स्त्री, मारुत, धूप और कर्म से क्लान्त हुए लोगों के लिए अनुपान के रूप में दूध अमृत के समान पथ्य है।
english: For those exhausted by fasting, travel, speaking, women, wind, sun and action (karma), milk as an after-drink is wholesome like amṛta (nectar).
notes: karman at the end of the compound may instead govern all the members ('by the acts of fasting, travel, ...'); it is given as a separate member. adhvan = road, travel on foot. māruta here is the physical wind among the exhausting factors (wind and sun), as in Sū 22. strī 'women' is translated literally.

hindi: कृशों की पुष्टि के लिए सुरा अनुपान के रूप में विहित है; स्थूल देह वालों की कृशता के लिए बाद में मधूदक प्रशस्त है।
english: For the lean, surā is prescribed as an after-drink for building up (puṣṭi); for the stout-bodied, for leanness (kārśya), honey-water is commended afterwards.
notes: anu is taken as the adverb 'afterwards' (i.e. as after-drink).

words.gloss: of those with weak digestive fire
by drowsiness, grief, fear and exhaustion
of those accustomed to madya and meat

hindi: मन्द अग्नि वालों के लिए, तन्द्रा, शोक, भय और क्लम से निद्रा-रहित लोगों के लिए, और मद्य तथा मांस के अभ्यस्त लोगों के लिए मद्य ही अनुशंसित है।
english: For those with weak digestive fire (agni), for those sleepless from drowsiness (tandrā), grief, fear and exhaustion, and for those accustomed to madya and meat, madya alone is recommended (as after-drink).
notes: The instrumental tandrā-śoka-bhaya-klamaiḥ is taken with anidrāṇām ('sleepless from ...'); it may instead name a separate group ('those afflicted by drowsiness, grief, fear and exhaustion'). madya kept Sanskrit as earlier in the chapter.

words.gloss: the actions and qualities of the after-drink
words.gram: m. acc. pl., tat-puruṣa containing dvandva
f. acc. sg., abstract (-tā) of sukha-pariṇāmin
f. acc. sg., abstract (-tā) of āśu-vyavāyin

hindi: अब अनुपान के कर्म और गुण कहेंगे। अनुपान तर्पण करता है, प्रसन्न करता है, ऊर्जा देता है, बृंहण करता है, पर्याप्ति उत्पन्न करता है, खाए हुए को नीचे बैठाता है, अन्न के संघात को तोड़ता है, मृदुता लाता है, क्लेदन करता है, पचाता है, और आहार का सुखपूर्वक परिणाम तथा शीघ्र व्यवायिता उत्पन्न करता है।
english: Now we shall explain the actions and qualities of the after-drink. The after-drink replenishes, gladdens, invigorates, nourishes, brings about satiation (paryāpti), makes what has been eaten settle down, breaks up the compact mass of food, produces softness, moistens, digests, and produces easy transformation (pariṇāma) and quick diffusion (vyavāyitā) of food.
notes: Prose line typed as a verse unit. tarpayati = replenishes (tarpaṇa), bṛṃhayati = nourishes (bṛṃhaṇa), kledayati = moistens (kleda = moistness). avasādayati literally 'makes sink'. vyavāyitā literally 'pervasiveness' (from vyavāyin 'pervading'); 'quick diffusion' is given. The final iti closes the passage and is not translated.
lines_deva: अथानुपानकर्मगुणान् प्रवक्ष्यामः अनुपानं तर्पयति, प्रीणयति, ऊर्जयति, बृंहयति, पर्याप्तिमभिनिर्वर्तयति, भुक्तमवसादयति, अन्नसङ्घातं भिनत्ति, मार्दवमापादयति, क्लेदयति, जरयति, सुखपरिणामितामाशुव्यवायितां चाहारस्योपजनयतीति
lines_iast: athānupānakarmaguṇān pravakṣyāmaḥ anupānaṃ tarpayati, prīṇayati, ūrjayati, bṛṃhayati, paryāptimabhinirvartayati, bhuktamavasādayati, annasaṅghātaṃ bhinatti, mārdavamāpādayati, kledayati, jarayati, sukhapariṇāmitāmāśuvyavāyitāṃ cāhārasyopajanayatīti

hindi: और यहाँ (श्लोक) है: हितकर अनुपान, ठीक से प्रयुक्त होने पर, मनुष्य का शीघ्र तर्पण करता है, आहार को सुखपूर्वक पचाता है, और आयु तथा बल के लिए (होता है)।
english: And here there is: a wholesome after-drink, properly used, quickly replenishes a man, digests food easily, and (serves) for life and strength.
notes: pacati literally 'cooks'. The datives āyuṣe ca balāya ca have no verb; '(serves)' is understood.
lines_deva: सुखं पचति चाहारमायुषे च बलाय च
lines_iast: sukhaṃ pacati cāhāramāyuṣe ca balāya ca

words.gloss: those possessed by Vāta in the upper body
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa, ppp. ā-√viś

words.gloss: those suffering from hiccup, dyspnoea and cough
those devoted to singing, speaking and study
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa, ppp. pra-√sañj

hindi: न ऊर्ध्व अंगों में मारुत से ग्रस्त, न हिक्का, श्वास और कास के रोगी, न गाने, बोलने और अध्ययन में लगे हुए, न छाती में क्षत वाले —
english: Not those possessed by Vāta (māruta) in the upper parts of the body, not those suffering from hiccup (hikkā), dyspnoea (śvāsa) and cough, not those devoted to singing, speaking and study, not those injured in the chest —

text_flags.why: possible: the subject must be nominative plural like kāsinaḥ, prasaktā(ḥ), kṣatāḥ in this verse and pibeyuḥ in 328; -āviṣṭāḥ loses its visarga before 'na' as -āviṣṭā, so the short final a looks like a slip
bhāṣya + adhyayana joins as bhāṣyādhyayana; the extra 'a' gives the half-line 17 syllables, with bhāṣyādhyayana it has 16

notes: SENTENCE: the verb (pibeyur udakaṃ bhuktvā 'should drink water after eating') is in 328. prasaktā is prasaktāḥ with the visarga dropped before n.

hindi: भोजन करके जल पीएँ; क्योंकि वह (जल) कण्ठ और छाती में स्थित होकर आहार से उत्पन्न स्नेह को नष्ट करके फिर दोष के लिए होता है।
english: — should drink water after eating; for that (water), staying in the throat and chest, destroys the unctuousness (sneha) born of food and becomes conducive to further doṣa.

text_flags.why: the place paired with uras 'chest' (cf. 'norasi kṣatāḥ' in 327) is kaṇṭha 'throat'; kaṇṭa 'thorn' gives no sense, ṭ for ṭh is a slip; syllable count unchanged

notes: SENTENCE: continues 327 (its subjects). bhūyaḥ may mean 'again' or 'more'; 'further' is given. doṣāya kalpate may mean 'leads to (aggravation of) the doṣas' or 'leads to harm'; the Sanskrit word is kept.

words.gloss: a part of food and drink

hindi: अन्न-पान का यह एक भाग कहा गया है जो प्रायः उपयोग में आता है; क्योंकि द्रव्यों को नामों से सम्पूर्णतः बताना सम्भव नहीं है।
english: This part of food and drink, which is mostly in use, has been stated; for it is not possible to indicate substances completely by names.

text_flags.why: 'kātsnrya' is not a Sanskrit word; the abstract of kṛtsna 'whole' is kārtsnya, and the r has been typed after the n; syllable count unchanged

notes: śakyam is used impersonally with dravyāṇi as the object of nirdeṣṭum.
lines_deva: द्रव्याणि न हि निर्देष्टुं शक्यं कात्स्न्र्येन नामभिः
lines_iast: dravyāṇi na hi nirdeṣṭuṃ śakyaṃ kātsnryena nāmabhiḥ

words.gloss: of those born in the region

words.gram: n. nom. sg., ppp. √vac with nañ

hindi: जैसे कुछ भी अनौषध नहीं है, (वैसे ही) देश में उत्पन्न लोगों के वचन के अनुसार, जो द्रव्य यहाँ नहीं कहा गया हो, वह-वह उसी प्रकार कहा जाना चाहिए।
english: Just as there is nothing that is not a medicine, so, according to the speech of the people born in the region, each substance that may not be stated here should be named in that way.
notes: nānauṣadham is split na + anauṣadham 'there is no non-medicine'; the split nānā-auṣadham 'various medicines' is grammatically possible but gives a weaker sense with kiṃcit. The second yathā is taken as 'according to' with deśajānāṃ vacaḥ. The correlation of the first yathā with tathā is loose.

hindi: चर, शरीर के अवयव, स्वभाव, धातु, क्रिया, लिङ्ग, प्रमाण, संस्कार और मात्रा — इसमें (इनकी) परीक्षा की जाती है।
english: Habitat (cara), body parts, own nature (svabhāva), the dhātus, activity (kriyā), sex (liṅga), size (pramāṇa), processing (saṃskāra) and measure (mātrā) are examined in this (matter).

text_flags.why: the ninth item of the list is the feminine noun mātrā, as the list is explained in this chunk ('mātrā kāraṇam uddiṣṭam' 340, 'mātrā cāgnim apekṣate' 341); the short final ā is a slip

notes: The list is the headings for the heaviness and lightness of foods explained in 332-341. liṅgaḥ is printed masculine; the word is normally neuter (liṅgam); kept as printed. asmin 'in this' is taken as the topic of heaviness and lightness (cf. 340, 343).
lines_deva: लिङ्गः प्रमाणं संस्कारो मात्र चास्मिन् परीक्ष्यते
lines_iast: liṅgaḥ pramāṇaṃ saṃskāro mātra cāsmin parīkṣyate

words.gloss: marsh, water, sky, dry land and the rest
those born in water and marsh
words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva of upapada tat-puruṣas

words.gloss: those moving in water and marsh

hindi: चर अनूप, जल, आकाश, धन्व आदि (स्थान) और भक्ष्य की व्यवस्था है; जो जल और अनूप में उत्पन्न हैं तथा जो जल और अनूप में विचरने वाले हैं,
english: Habitat (cara) is marsh, water, sky, dry land (dhanvan) and the rest, (and) the arrangement of food (bhakṣyasaṃvidhi); those which are born in water and marsh, and those which move in water and marsh,
notes: SENTENCE: continues into 333 (sarve te guravaḥ smṛtāḥ). bhakṣyasaṃvidhi is taken as 'what the animal eats', which 333 explains (gurubhakṣya, laghubhakṣya); the exact sense of saṃvidhi is not certain. anūpa = marsh, dhanvan = dry region as in the glossary.

hindi: और जो प्राणी गुरु भक्ष्य वाले हैं, वे सब गुरु माने गए हैं; किन्तु लघु भक्ष्य वाले, धन्व में उत्पन्न और धन्व में विचरने वाले लघु हैं।
english: and the creatures which eat heavy food — all of them are considered heavy; but those that eat light food, those born in dry land and those moving in dry land are light.
notes: SENTENCE: the subjects in 332b belong to 'sarve te guravaḥ smṛtāḥ' here. sattva here = living creature (not mind). The plural adjectives dhanvajā(ḥ) and dhanvacāriṇaḥ are taken with laghavaḥ.
lines_deva: गुरुभक्ष्याश्च ये सत्त्वाः सर्वे ते गुरवः स्मृताः
lines_iast: gurubhakṣyāśca ye sattvāḥ sarve te guravaḥ smṛtāḥ

words.gloss: thigh, head, shoulder and the rest

hindi: शरीर के अवयव, वैसे ही, सक्थि, सिर, स्कन्ध आदि हैं; सक्थि के मांस से स्कन्ध गुरु है, उससे क्रोड, उससे सिर।
english: The body parts are, likewise, the thigh, head, shoulder and the rest; the shoulder is heavier than the thigh meat, the kroḍa (breast) than that, the head than that.
notes: guru with the ablative has comparative force ('heavier than'); guruḥ is understood with kroḍa and śiras. kroḍa may mean breast or flank; kept Sanskrit with 'breast'.

hindi: दोनों वृषण, चर्म, मेढ्र, दोनों श्रोणि, दोनों वृक्क, यकृत्, गुद और मध्य (भाग) तथा अस्थि — इन्हें यथास्व मांस से अधिक गुरु जानना चाहिए।
english: The two testicles, skin, penis, the two hips, the two kidneys, liver and anus (guda), and the middle (part) and bone — one should know (these) to be heavier than the flesh, each according to its own (kind).
notes: madhyamasthi is split madhyam + asthi ('the middle part and bone'); it could also be read as madhyam asthi 'the middle bone'. The words of line a are taken as accusative objects of vidyāt (the forms are the same as the nominative); gurutaram (n. sg.) is predicated of them all. yathāsvam is taken as 'compared with the flesh of the same animal'. śroṇī may also be the singular of the ī-stem śroṇī 'hip, pelvis'; the dual of śroṇi is given.
lines_deva: वृषणौ चर्म मेढ्रं च श्रोणी वृक्कौ यकृद्गुदम्
lines_iast: vṛṣaṇau carma meḍhraṃ ca śroṇī vṛkkau yakṛdgudam

hindi: स्वभाव से मुद्ग लघु होते हैं, वैसे ही लाव और कपिञ्जल; स्वभाव से माष गुरु होते हैं, वैसे ही वराह और महिष।
english: By nature mudgas are light, likewise lāvas and kapiñjalas; by nature māṣas are heavy, likewise boars and buffaloes.

text_flags.why: possible: metre of the odd pāda: syllables 5-7 gha-vo-mu = light-heavy-light, not allowed; with mud- the 7th is heavy (light-heavy-heavy); sense: a pulse paired with māṣāḥ in line b; 'muga' is not a Sanskrit word

notes: mudga: green gram; māṣa: black gram (plain names, kept Sanskrit in the translations). lāva and kapiñjala kept Sanskrit (no identification).

hindi: रक्त आदि धातुओं में उत्तरोत्तर (प्रत्येक को) गुरु जानना चाहिए; जो प्राणी बहुत क्रियाशील हैं, वे आलसी (प्राणियों) से विशिष्ट हैं।
english: Of the dhātus beginning with blood, one should know (each) successive one to be heavy(-ier); living beings that are very active are superior to the sluggish ones.
notes: gurum (m. acc. sg.) is taken distributively ('each later one heavy'); the comparative sense comes from yathottaram. viśiṣyante 'are superior' is taken as superior in lightness (the topic of kriyā in 331); the text does not say in what respect. The order of the dhātus is not given in this chunk.

hindi: लिङ्ग के सामान्य (विचार) में पुरुषों का गौरव और स्त्रियों का तो लाघव है; अपनी जाति में बड़े प्रमाण वाले गुरु और अन्यथा लघु होते हैं।
english: As to sex (liṅga) in general, heaviness belongs to males, but lightness to females; within their own species those of large size (pramāṇa) are heavy, otherwise (they are) light.
notes: liṅgasāmānye is literally 'in the commonness of sex'; it is taken as 'as to sex in general' (perhaps 'among animals of one kind'); the exact sense is uncertain. puṃs/strī here are male and female animals.
lines_deva: गौरवं लिङ्गसामान्ये पुंसां स्त्रीणां तु लाघवम्
lines_iast: gauravaṃ liṅgasāmānye puṃsāṃ strīṇāṃ tu lāghavam

hindi: संस्कार से गुरु (द्रव्यों) का विपर्यय-सहित लाघव जानना चाहिए; जैसे व्रीहि से लाजा होते हैं, और सक्तु की पकी हुई पिण्डिकाएँ।
english: One should know the lightness of heavy (substances) from processing (saṃskāra), together with the reverse: as lājā (parched grain) would come from rice (vrīhi), and cooked balls of saktu.

text_flags.why: 'saṃskrāra' is not a word; the same heading is printed saṃskāro in 331 of this chunk; the extra r is a slip; syllable count unchanged

notes: The two examples illustrate the two directions: rice made into lājā becomes lighter, saktu made into cooked balls becomes heavier (the reverse); this pairing is inferred from saviparyayam and is not stated. vrīheḥ may also be genitive. lājā, saktu kept Sanskrit.
lines_deva: व्रीहेर्लाजा यथा च स्युः सक्तूनां सिद्धपिण्डिकाः
lines_iast: vrīherlājā yathā ca syuḥ saktūnāṃ siddhapiṇḍikāḥ

hindi: गुरु (द्रव्यों) के अल्प ग्रहण में और लघु (द्रव्यों) के अति सेवन में, द्रव्यों के गुरु-लाघव में मात्रा कारण कही गई है।
english: In taking a small amount of heavy (substances) and in excessive use of light ones, measure (mātrā) is declared the cause in the heaviness and lightness of substances.
notes: uddiṣṭam agrees with kāraṇam (n.), not with mātrā (f.).

hindi: गुरु (द्रव्यों) का अल्प (भाग) लेना चाहिए, लघु (द्रव्यों) की तृप्ति (तक सेवन) इष्ट है; द्रव्य मात्रा की अपेक्षा रखते हैं और मात्रा अग्नि की अपेक्षा रखती है।
english: Of heavy (substances) a little should be taken; of light ones satisfaction is desired. Substances depend on measure (mātrā), and measure depends on the digestive fire (agni).

words.gloss: by the fuel of food and drink

hindi: बल, आरोग्य, आयु और प्राण अग्नि में प्रतिष्ठित हैं; और अग्नि अन्न-पान रूपी ईंधन से जलती है और अन्यथा बुझ जाती है।
english: Strength, health, life and the vital breaths (prāṇa) are established in agni (digestive fire); and agni blazes with the fuel of food and drink, and otherwise goes out.
notes: pratiṣṭhitāḥ agrees with the nearest subject prāṇāḥ. vyeti literally 'goes away, perishes'.

hindi: गुरु-लाघव का यह विचार प्रायः अल्प बल वाले, मन्द क्रिया वाले, अस्वस्थ, सुकुमार और सुख के अभ्यस्त लोगों के प्रति है।
english: This consideration of heaviness and lightness is mostly with regard to those of little strength, of little activity, unhealthy, delicate and accustomed to comfort.

text_flags.why: 'alapav' is not a word; with alpa- (cf. alpāgnīnām 324, alpādāne 340) the half-line has 16 syllables, the printed form gives 17

notes: The verse is contrasted with 344 (those for whom the consideration is not necessary).

hindi: जो मनुष्य दीप्त अग्नि वाले, खर आहार वाले, कर्म में नित्य लगे रहने वाले और बड़े उदर वाले हैं, उनके प्रति गुरु-लाघव का विचार आवश्यक नहीं है।
english: Men who have a kindled digestive fire, eat rough (khara) food, are constantly engaged in action (karma) and have large stomachs — with regard to them heaviness and lightness need not necessarily be considered.
notes: mahodara here is a bahuvrīhi 'having a large stomach', not the disease udara. khara = rough as in the glossary.
lines_deva: ये नराः प्रति तांश्चिन्त्यं नावश्यं गुरुलाघवम्
lines_iast: ye narāḥ prati tāṃścintyaṃ nāvaśyaṃ gurulāghavam

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. caus. vi-√car

hindi: मनुष्य सावधान होकर, मात्रा और काल का विचार करते हुए, अन्न-पान रूपी हितकर समिधाओं से नित्य अन्तरग्नि में आहुति दे।
english: A man, attentive and considering measure and time, should always make offering into the inner fire with wholesome fuel-sticks (samidh) of food and drink.
notes: hitābhiḥ (f.) agrees with samidbhiḥ in line b. juhuyāt 'should offer (as an oblation)'.

words.gloss: one who has installed the fire

hindi: जो आहिताग्नि सदा पथ्य (पदार्थों) की अन्तरग्नि में आहुति देता है, प्रतिदिन ब्रह्म का जप करता है और दान देता है,
english: He who, having installed the fire (āhitāgni), always offers wholesome things into the inner fire, who day by day recites brahman (the sacred text) and gives,
notes: SENTENCE: the relative clause continues into 347 (naraṃ ... bhajante nāmayāḥ). divase divase = every day. brahma japati: recites the sacred text (brahman). dadāti without object: gives (gifts).
lines_deva: दिवसे दिवसे ब्रह्म जपत्यथ ददाति च
lines_iast: divase divase brahma japatyatha dadāti ca

hindi: निःश्रेयस में लगे हुए, पान और भोजन में सात्म्य को जानने वाले उस मनुष्य को अन्तर के बिना कोई रोग नहीं घेरते, भावी (रोग) भी नहीं।
english: — that man, devoted to the highest good (niḥśreyasa) and knowing what is suitable (sātmya) in drink and food, no diseases approach, not even those destined to come (bhāvin), except through some opening (antara).
notes: SENTENCE: continues 346 (its relative clause describes this man). antarād ṛte is literally 'without an interval/opening'; it may mean 'except through a lapse' or 'except after a lapse of time'; the exact sense is uncertain.

hindi: हितकर भोजन करने वाला, जितात्मा, सज्जनों द्वारा सम्मानित जन्तु छत्तीस हजार रातें रोग-रहित होकर जीता है।
english: A person (jantu) who eats wholesome food, self-controlled and esteemed by the good, lives free from illness for thirty-six thousand nights.

text_flags.why: grammar: final ṣ of ṣaṣ becomes ṭ before the voiceless t (ṣaṭ-triṃśat); ḍ before t is not a valid sandhi; syllable count unchanged

notes: ṣaṭtriṃśatam ... sahasrāṇi is an accusative of duration.

hindi: प्राणियों के प्राण अन्न हैं; लोक अन्न की ओर दौड़ता है। वर्ण, प्रसाद, सुस्वरता, जीवन, प्रतिभा, सुख —
english: Food is the vital breath (prāṇa) of living beings; the world runs after food. Complexion, clarity (prasāda), a good voice, life, intelligence (pratibhā), happiness —
notes: SENTENCE: the list in line b continues in 350a (sarvam anne pratiṣṭhitam). prāṇabhṛt literally 'breath-bearer'. prāṇāḥ (pl.) is predicated of annam (sg.).
lines_deva: वर्णः प्रसादः सौस्वर्यं जीवितं प्रतिभा सुखम्
lines_iast: varṇaḥ prasādaḥ sausvaryaṃ jīvitaṃ pratibhā sukham

hindi: तुष्टि, पुष्टि, बल, मेधा — सब अन्न में प्रतिष्ठित है। जीविका के लिए जो लौकिक कर्म है, और स्वर्ग-प्राप्ति के लिए जो वैदिक (कर्म) है,
english: contentment, plumpness (puṣṭi), strength, intellect (medhā) — all is established in food. The worldly action (karma) that is for livelihood, and the Vedic (action) that is for going to heaven,

text_flags.why: grammar: 'ya' is not a form of the relative; yat + ca gives yacca, as printed 'yaccoktaṃ' in 351 of this chunk

notes: SENTENCE: line a completes 349b; line b begins a sentence completed in 351a (tac cāpy anne pratiṣṭhitam).
lines_deva: लौकिकं कर्म यद्वृत्तौ स्वर्गतौ यच वैदिकम्
lines_iast: laukikaṃ karma yadvṛttau svargatau yaca vaidikam

words.gloss: the qualities of food and drink

hindi: और अपवर्ग के लिए कर्म में जो कहा गया है, वह भी अन्न में प्रतिष्ठित है। यहाँ श्लोक है: अग्र्य (द्रव्यों) सहित अन्न-पान के गुण, निश्चित बारह वर्ग,
english: and what is stated about action for liberation (apavarga), that too is established in food. Here, the verse: the qualities of food and drink together with the foremost (agrya), the twelve groups determined,
notes: GROUPING: line a closes the sentence begun in 350b; 'tatra ślokaḥ' and line c open the summary verse, which continues in 352 (351c + 352ab form the summary of three half-lines). karmāpavarge is taken as 'in (the matter of) action for liberation'; it could also be a dvandva 'in action and in liberation'. sāgryāḥ 'with the foremost (agrya) items' is taken with annapānaguṇāḥ.

words.gloss: the summary of heaviness and lightness
in the Annapānavidhi (rule of food and drink)

hindi: गुणों सहित अनुपान, गुरु-लाघव का संग्रह — (यह) अन्नपानविधि में कहा गया है; उसकी विशेष रूप से परीक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: the after-drinks with their qualities, the summary of heaviness and lightness — (this) has been stated in the Annapānavidhi (rule of food and drink); it should be examined in particular.

text_flags.why: anupāna is printed correctly throughout this chunk (321, 325, 326); the extra 'a' gives the quarter 9 syllables, with anupānāni it has 8

notes: SENTENCE: completes the summary verse begun in 351c. annapānavidhi is the name of this chapter (see the colophon P2).

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में अन्नपानविधि नामक सत्ताईसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna), the twenty-seventh chapter named Annapānavidhi.
notes: Chapter colophon (prose), verbless.
